subject: Close runway sequencing and acceptance gating for SagePoint pilot
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Miriam Cole <miriam.cole@sagepoint.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-02T09:15:00Z
Subject: Initial MAP and sequencing proposal for SagePoint pilot

Miriam — thanks again for the time earlier. Per our call, I pulled together a simple mutual action plan that aligns evaluation milestones to procurement/legal gating so we can get the pilot live without blocking on full contract negotiation. Attachment: SagePoint_MAP_v1.xlsx (MAP with dates).

High-level proposal (single-pager):
- Week 1 (Aug 9–13): Security questionnaire + SOC2 evidence exchange (you flagged this as priority)
- Week 2 (Aug 16–20): Pilot evaluation kickoff (1-week technical trial, test dataset only)
- Week 3 (Aug 23–27): Pilot wrap, final acceptance test; procurement drafts order form and PO
- Week 4 (Aug 30–Sep 3): Sign MSA + DPA + Order Form OR sign MSA with order form contingent sign (see sequencing options below)

Sequencing notes (options):
A) Parallel legal + procurement: Legal reviews MSA/DPA in Week 1–2, procurement issues PO in Week 3, signature in Week 4. This shortens runway but requires legal resourcing to prioritize redlines.
B) Pilot-first, paper-after (low-risk pilot): Start the pilot under a limited acceptance letter/statement of work and finalize full MSA/DPA before production. Order form is executed after MSA is signed.

We also want to avoid the common blocker where procurement insists on signed DPA language before issuing a PO. If SagePoint can issue a purchase order contingent on a standard DPA template, we can proceed faster. Karthik & Laura — can you confirm internal appetite for option A vs B and whether legal can commit a turnaround on redlines in 3 business days?

Action items for today:
- Redwood: share editable redline-ready MSA + suggested DPA clause for pilot (I attached redlines_MSA_SagePoint_v3.docx).
- SagePoint: confirm procurement lead and PO timing; let us know if a contingent PO is possible.

Thanks — looking to keep this tight so the pilot momentum stays intact.

– Jonas
Head of Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

---

From: Miriam Cole <miriam.cole@sagepoint.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jordan Lake <jordan.lake@sagepoint.com>
Date: 2026-08-03T13:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Initial MAP and sequencing proposal for SagePoint pilot

Jonas — thanks, this is helpful and clear. A couple quick notes from procurement/legal side: 

- Procurement: Our procurement lead (Jordan Lake) is on copy. Typical PO lead time for pilots is 7–10 business days once procurement has the order form + pricing. We prefer a PO before any paid pilot, but we can be flexible for a limited proof-of-concept under a signed SOW or acceptance letter.
- Legal: Our counsel asked whether the DPA you attached is your standard template or whether we should expect substantive changes. We will need an explicit data handling clause for test data retention (30 days post-eval) and a clause addressing KV cache residency for the pilot.

Question for Redwood: can you accept a signed order form that references an MSA to be finalized within 30 days? If not, we will need the MSA to be signed up front. Also please share the DPA text so our legal can review.

I will coordinate with Jordan and get back with procurement timing by EOD tomorrow.

Miriam
Director, Biology Ops
SagePoint Therapeutics

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-08-04T10:47:00Z
Subject: Re: Initial MAP and sequencing proposal for SagePoint pilot — internal alignment

Jonas/Karthik — quick internal note after reading Miriam's reply and scanning the redlines doc. Key points and recommended play: 

1) Risk vs velocity tradeoff
- Option A (parallel): fastest to pilot but requires legal to prioritize; acceptable if the customer is comfortable with a contingent PO.
- Option B (pilot-first SOW): safest from a legal standpoint; slower to revenue but less procurement friction.

2) Suggested hybrid:
- Sign a short pilot SOW (1 page) that covers scope, price cap, and data handling (30-day retention), and references the MSA/DPA to be signed within 30 days.
- Procurement issues a PO referencing the SOW and notes the MSA signature deadline. This keeps procurement comfortable and lets engineering start.

3) Action items for our side (I can own coordinating legal):
- Finalize a one-page SOW template from orderform_template.pdf and push DPA appendix with explicit KV cache language.
- Ask legal for a 48–72 hour turnaround on redlines to the MSA if we mark the deal as pilot-priority — I will escalate if needed.

4) Dependencies and blockers to call out to the customer:
- If SagePoint insists on MSA+DPA signed before any pilot activity, adjust MAP dates by +2 weeks.
- If procurement needs a PO before field access, we can agree a capped PO against the SOW.

I attached redlines_MSA_SagePoint_v3.docx with inline suggestions (major comment on indemnity carve-outs and data residency).

If you want, I can draft the one-page SOW and a short email template for Miriam clarifying the hybrid approach and the specific MSA clauses we will need to finalize.

— Laura
VP, Product + Legal Liaison
Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Close runway sequencing and acceptance gating for SagePoint pilot — proposed commitments

Miriam/Jordan — appreciate the quick turnaround. Based on internal alignment (see Laura's note) here's a concise commitment we can all sign to and put into the MAP: 

Proposed commitments (final MAP attached) — SagePoint pilot (limited access):
- Redwood will deliver a 1-week pilot environment starting Aug 16 conditioned on a signed one-page SOW and a PO referencing that SOW.
- The full MSA + DPA will be executed within 30 calendar days of the SOW signature; Order Form will be signed no later than the MSA execution date.
- Data retention for pilot test data: 30 days post-eval; KV cache residency: evict within 48 hours of test completion unless specifically requested otherwise by SagePoint.
- If the MSA is materially redlined (beyond agreed carve-outs), both parties agree to a 14-day extension to resolve (no autopause of pilot during the extension unless SagePoint requests pause).

Next steps for you:
1) Jordan — confirm that your procurement team can issue a PO referencing a one-page SOW and give an estimated issue date (target Aug 12).
2) Miriam — confirm the pilot scope in the MAP attachment and confirm any additional data handling constraints.

I have uploaded the one-page SOW + updated MAP: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/HS-48392 (see files + DocuSign link). DocuSign placeholder: https://docusign.com/templates/abcdef123456

If you reply with "Agree" we will prepare the DocuSign packet and Laura will shepherd legal redlines on a 48–72 hour SLA. Looking forward to locking this in and starting the evaluation.

Thanks —
Jonas
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
